overview: Brent crude settled at $108.82 on Wednesday, pulling back from a five-month high as Russia's Vladimir Putin agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine — a development analysts said could unlock tight global diesel supplies. WTI fell to $97.15. Support remained from Strait of Hormuz disruptions, with Kpler data showing crude flows at 11.6 million barrels a day, roughly 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline. UKMTO reported at least 12 ships attacked in the week to October 16, the highest weekly total since the war began, including a container ship that sank and a new small-boat RPG attack type. US crude inventories fell 3.06 million barrels, triple the expected draw, and the Energy Department offered to lend up to a third of its emergency heating oil reserve to ease diesel pressure. Newcastle coal held near $151 a tonne.

Gold edged up to $4,134 as the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.13%, though a 20-year auction drew 5.469%, the highest for that maturity since 1986. Silver slipped to $57.50 and platinum fell 1.5% to $1,635. Palladium dropped to $1,088, its lowest since September 2025 and now down 17% over four weeks. December wheat fell 15 cents to $6.28, the sharpest one-day loss in three weeks, while corn ticked up a cent to $4.63. Bitcoin surged to $84,400 after JPMorgan issued its first-ever 10% annual BTC price forecast and US spot ETFs attracted roughly $550 million in inflows over 48 hours. Ethereum rose to $2,476. Tesla and Meta reported earnings after the close.

watchItems.title: Tesla & Meta earnings after Wednesday close
watchItems.text: Tesla reported 486,532 Q3 deliveries, above estimates of about 461,000. EPS estimates ranged widely from $0.30 to $0.70, with margins and Full Self-Driving commentary expected to matter more than the headline. Meta consensus revenue is about $63 billion, up 23% year-over-year. Results could set the tone for AI-linked names after the Nasdaq's worst week since June.

watchItems.title: FOMC, Oct 27–28
watchItems.text: The Fed remains in its communications blackout until October 29. The 20-year Treasury auction drew 5.469%, the highest since 1986, underscoring persistent inflation concerns. September CPI at 3.7% and crude above $100 keep the door open for an October rate move. Q3 GDP and September PCE inflation land next week ahead of the decision.

watchItems.title: Hormuz attacks at wartime high
watchItems.text: UKMTO reported at least 12 ships attacked in one week, the highest weekly total since the war began. A container ship sank, and Iran introduced small-boat RPG attacks as a new tactic. Crude flows are at 68% of the pre-war baseline. Iran's acting Defence Minister said Tehran intends to continue strikes. Mediators including Pakistan and Qatar see no breakthrough soon.

watchItems.title: Russia–Ukraine peace talks could ease diesel crunch
watchItems.text: Putin agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as early as November. Analysts say a deal could unlock tight global diesel supplies — the US offered to lend nearly a third of its emergency heating oil reserve this week. Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil infrastructure have also added to global supply pressure.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold edged up 0.4% to about $4,134 on Wednesday, recovering from early-session lows near $4,108 after the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.13%. A 20-year auction drew 5.469%, the highest for that maturity since 1986, reflecting persistent inflation concerns. Gold remains about 26% below its January record near $5,608.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver slipped about 0.7% to $57.50 on Wednesday, giving back part of Tuesday's gains as precious metals broadly softened. The metal is down roughly 13% on the month but the Silver Institute projects a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit. Silver remains about 53% below its late-January record near $121.6.

desk.name: Oil
desk.sum: Brent crude settled at $108.82, pulling back from a five-month high after Russia agreed to resume peace talks with Ukraine — a development analysts said could ease the global diesel crunch. WTI fell to $97.15. Support remained from Hormuz disruptions, with Kpler putting crude flows at 11.6 million barrels a day, about 68% of the pre-war baseline. US crude inventories fell 3.06 million barrels, triple the expected draw.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper eased to $6.53 per pound on Wednesday, weighed by a firmer dollar and softer risk sentiment. The metal is down 2.3% on the month but remains near record territory, trading about 4.7% below its September high of $6.85. BHP's recent report of a 19% drop in September-quarter copper output continues to underpin the supply side.

desk.name: Coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal edged up to about $151 a tonne, holding near three-year highs. The IEA expects global coal demand to rise 1.2% to a record 8.94 billion tonnes this year as the Hormuz gas shock drives Asian and European utilities back to coal. Indonesia's tightened export rules and strong pre-winter buying from Japan and South Korea continue to support prices. Coal is up over 40% year-to-date.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum fell 1.5% to $1,635 on Wednesday, resuming its downtrend after a brief bounce earlier in the week. The metal is down about 9% on the month as the WPIC forecasts an 18% drop in total platinum demand this year. Platinum remains about 9% below its September levels.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium dropped 1.6% to $1,088, its lowest level since September 2025. The metal is now down 17% over four weeks and more than 25% lower on the year. EV adoption continues to erode catalytic-converter demand, and Russia's sanctions waiver could ease tight supply from Norilsk Nickel.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz crisis reached a new intensity, with UKMTO reporting at least 12 ships attacked in the week to October 16 — the highest weekly total since the war began. A container ship sank after being hit and Iran introduced small-boat RPG attacks as a new tactic. Kpler data puts crude flows at 11.6 million barrels a day, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline. Iran's acting Defence Minister said Tehran intends to continue strikes. Mediators including Pakistan and Qatar see no diplomatic breakthrough soon.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn ticked up about a cent to $4.63 on Wednesday, pausing after a multi-day decline. The corn harvest is advancing rapidly in dry weather and is nearing the five-year average pace. Corn is down about 15% on the month as fund liquidation and harvest pressure persist.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: CBOT December wheat dropped 15 cents to $6.28 on Wednesday, the sharpest one-day loss in three weeks. Winter wheat planting is catching up after a slow start, and weak export demand continues to compound selling pressure. Wheat is down about 14% on the month but remains more than 25% higher year-to-date.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: November soybeans eased 3 cents to $12.45 on Wednesday, pressured by advancing harvest and technical selling. The US soybean harvest continues to run ahead of the five-year average and is pointing to a record crop.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin rose about 2% to $84,400 on Wednesday after JPMorgan issued its first-ever 10% annual BTC price forecast. US spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted roughly $550 million in inflows over 48 hours, reversing October's earlier outflow trend. Ethereum rose to $2,476. The Fear & Greed Index sits at 48 (neutral) ahead of the FOMC's October 27–28 meeting.
